cap_core_min_per_run.basis: Sanaa 2026-09-03 18:00Z item 2: a hard per-run cap set BY THE TEAM at ~3x its own estimate. Arithmetic shown in prereg section 8.2: B0_L1 estimate 4.376 core-min x3 = 13.128 -> cap 13.20; B0_L3 estimate 32.980 x3 = 98.939 -> cap 99.00.
cap_core_min_per_run.which_estimate_the_3x_multiplies: For the two C5 runs the x3 multiplies the NO-SPEED-UP estimate (the measured baseline cost at that level), NOT C5's extrapolated estimate. DISCLOSED, NOT BURIED, and ACCEPTED BY THE SUPERVISOR ON THE RECORD at prereg Amendment A1.2: a cap set at 3x an estimate that already assumes the hypothesis is TRUE would guarantee a censored run precisely when the hypothesis is FALSE -- the one outcome this rung exists to detect, and exactly how T25R5 lost C2 and C3. Sanaa's law fixes the cap to the team's own estimate and does not say WHICH estimate. BOTH estimates are registered in advance (prereg 8.1 and 8.2), which is what makes this defensible rather than a choice made later.

cap_enforcement: THE LAUNCHER'S `timeout` WRAPPER IS THE ONLY THING THAT STOPS THIS RUN. scripts/queue_runner.py REPORTS a cap overrun and does NOT kill. The cap therefore binds only through the arithmetic timeout_s = cap_core_min * 60 / ranks, and run_one_t25R6a.sh REFUSES at pre-flight if the registered timeout_s does not equal that product (13.20*60/2 = 396 s at L1, exit 84), REFUSES a --timeout not equal to the registered timeout_s (exit 83), and REFUSES --ranks != 2 (exit 82). A cap nothing enforces is not a cap.

two_ceilings_are_different_instruments: The 230 core-min cap here is a GUARD this team set on this run. They are never added together and the first is never licence against the second. Checked and reported: 230 is 1.15 % of 20,000, so the hazard does not arise here.

_one_entry_not_four_and_why: THIS RUNG IS A TIMING MEASUREMENT. G-T6a is computed from ExecutionTime RATIOS, so two cases running concurrently would contaminate the exact quantity being measured. Prereg section 10 step 4 registers the runs as sequential on T25R5 Addendum D1.3's protocol -- a protocol T25R5's own contention episode proved necessary. Four independent queue entries could be picked up on the same tick, so the sequence is enforced inside run_seq_t25R6a.sh, in ONE process, rather than hoped for from the scheduler. Registered order: B0_L1, C5_L1, B0_L3, C5_L3, baselines first at each level so a missing baseline is found before its arm spends anything.
_age_guard_scope_disclosed: Because this entry drives four cases, `cwd` is the RUN directory and not a case directory, so the validator's AGE-GUARD clause inspects the run directory rather than each case. THAT IS A WEAKER READING THAN USUAL AND IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED. The real per-case guard is in the launcher: run_one_t25R6a.sh REFUSES (exit 92) if the case holds `0/` and REFUSES (exit 93) if it holds any numeric time directory, and it creates `0/` itself and touches `0/module/T` LAST so that file dates the run allowed to produce the answer. Verified on disk at filing: each of B0_L1, C5_L1, B0_L3, C5_L3 contains exactly `0.orig`, `constant` and `system` -- no `0/`, no time directory, no processor*.

_completion_and_freeze_markers: run_seq_t25R6a.sh calls mark_done_t25R6a.py, which applies rule 4 IMPORTED FROM THE FROZEN GRADER (one definition of completion in this rung) and writes DONE.<CASE> carrying a `finished_utc=` line from the run's own stamp. This is deliberate: scripts/check_comparator_freeze.py dates a comparator's freeze against the earliest completion marker of the cases it grades, and T25R5_LINSOLVER_runs/ carries NO DONE.* marker at all, so all three of its graders sit in the unjudged NO-MARKERS state. mark_done is DEFAULT-DENY -- an incomplete case gets NO marker, because a marker saying done about a case that is not done would corrupt every freeze judgment later dated against it.
_cap_stop_is_a_bound_not_a_disqualificat: prereg section 7.3. An rc 124 yields a CENSORED wall factor with a known upper bound f < ExecutionTime(B0_level)/timeout_level; the grader computes Sigma CAP at that bound, returns GATE FAIL if the bound still breaches 20,000 (a bound that fails is a decision) and NOT A RESULT otherwise. A CENSORED RUN CAN NEVER PRODUCE A PASS. The sequential driver CONTINUES past a cap stop so the remaining levels are still measured, and STOPS on a launcher refusal (rc 80-96) because that means the case was never eligible. Note that Sanaa's ~3x cap law makes censoring almost impossible here: the smallest measurable wall factor is 131.28/396 = 0.3315 at L1 and 989.39/2970 = 0.3331 at L3, so a C5 three times SLOWER than the baseline is still MEASURED rather than disqualified. T25R5's x1.5 caps could not say that.
_what_this_entry_does_not_authorise: NO LADDER LAUNCHES ON ANY OUTCOME OF THIS RUNG, a G-T6a PASS INCLUDED (prereg 5.1 carried forward in force, and 7.4). Sigma CAP is the ladder's x4 TIMEOUT ALLOWANCE under the assumption that the 40-step RAMP wall factor holds for the whole run; 40 steps is 0.34 % of the shortest ladder run and it is the ramp, not the soak. The assumption is UNMEASURED and this rung does not test it. On GATE FAIL the rung reports the measured number and STOPS; a widening request is a desk item for Sanaa and is decided by nobody in this lab. This registration pre-registers NO widening and grants none.
